comparisons.peer_topic: Net Operating Losses and Tax Credits Carryforwards
comparisons.peer_summary: As of Dec 28, 2024, the Company had $134 million in U.S. federal and $362 million in state NOLs, with federal NOLs expiring between 2025-2037 or having no expiration, and state NOLs expiring through 2043; additional credits include $12 million federal (expiring 2037-2042), $804 million state (expiring 2025-2039, except CA R&D), and $620 million Canadian credits (expiring 2028-2044).
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and AVGO disclose specific U.S. state and foreign Net Operating Loss (NOL) carryforwards and expiration timelines. AVGO holds $126 million in U.S. state NOLs and $92 million in foreign NOLs expiring from fiscal 2025, alongside $2,176 million in state R&D credits. In contrast, AMD holds larger state NOLs ($362 million) but also significant federal NOLs ($134 million, with $107 million having no expiration), and its state credits ($804 million) expire between 2025-2039. AVGO's disclosure focuses on state/foreign NOLs and state credits, whereas AMD provides a broader breakdown including federal NOLs and credits with varying expiration profiles.

sentences.text: As of November 3, 2024, we had tax effected U.S. state net operating loss carryforwards of $126 million and foreign net operating loss carryforwards of $92 million, all of which expire in various years beginning in fiscal year 2025.
We had $2,176 million of state research and development tax credits which begin to expire in fiscal year 2025.
The Company's U.S. federal and state net operating losses (NOLs) carryforwards as of December 28, 2024, were $134 million and $362 million, respectively.

NOLs may be subject to limitations by the Internal Revenue Code and similar provisions. $27 million of U.S. federal NOLs will expire between 2025 and 2037, and $107 million of federal NOLs have no expiration date.
The federal tax credits of $12 million will expire at various dates between 2037 and 2042.
The state tax return credits of $804 million will expire at various dates between 2025 and 2039, except for the California R&D credit, which does not expire.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the company had $279 million in federal and $2.7 billion in non-US net operating loss carryforwards; the majority have no expiration date, while the remainder expire through 2040.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intels and AVGO disclose the status of their Net Operating Loss (NOL) carryforwards. AVGO reports $126 million in U.S. state NOLs and $92 million in foreign NOLs beginning to expire in fiscal 2025. Intel reports a much larger volume of NOLs, with $279 million in federal and $2.7 billion in non-US NOLs, but notes that the majority have no expiration date, with only the remainder expiring through 2040. This highlights a key difference: AVGO's disclosed NOLs are expiring soon (starting 2025), while Intel's are largely indefinite.

comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred tax assets and valuation allowance assessment
comparisons.peer_summary: The company maintains a valuation allowance of $593 million against net deferred tax assets as of August 29, 2024 (up from $528 million in 2023), primarily for U.S. state and Malaysia carryforwards, with changes driven by management's assessment of the realizability of tax credits and net operating losses.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and AVGO discuss the realizability of tax attributes (NOLs and credits) and associated valuation allowances. AVGO discloses specific expiring amounts for state NOLs ($126 million) and R&D credits ($2,176 million) starting in fiscal 2025. Micron discloses a valuation allowance of $593 million against net deferred tax assets as of August 29, 2024, specifically for carryforwards in U.S. states and Malaysia, driven by management's assessment that it is 'more likely than not' that some will not be realized. While AVGO lists the gross expiring assets, Micron focuses on the allowance reserved against them due to realizability concerns.

sentences.text: As of November 3, 2024, we had tax effected U.S. state net operating loss carryforwards of $126 million and foreign net operating loss carryforwards of $92 million, all of which expire in various years beginning in fiscal year 2025.
We had $2,176 million of state research and development tax credits which begin to expire in fiscal year 2025.
We assess positive and negative evidence for each jurisdiction to determine whether it is more likely than not that existing deferred tax assets will be realized.

As of August 29, 2024, and August 31, 2023, we had a valuation allowance of $593 million and $528 million, respectively, against our net deferred tax assets, primarily related to carryforwards in U.S. states and Malaysia.

Changes in 2024 in the valuation allowance were due to adjustments based on management's assessment of the realizability of tax credits, allowances and net operating losses based on a level that is more likely than not to be realized.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of January 28, 2024, the company held U.S. federal, state, and foreign net operating loss carryforwards totaling $1.018 billion, with U.S. federal and state portions expiring in 2026 and 2025 respectively; federal capital loss carryforwards of $1.4 billion expire in 2025; federal research tax credits of $31 million expire in 2025; and state research tax credits of $1.6 billion are mostly indefinite.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AVGO disclose specific U.S. state and federal/foreign NOL carryforwards and research tax credit expiration schedules. AVGO holds $126 million in state NOLs and $2,176 million in state R&D credits expiring from fiscal 2025. NVIDIA holds $342 million in state NOLs (expiring 2025) and $315 million in federal NOLs (expiring 2026), along with $31 million in federal R&D credits (expiring 2025) and $1.6 billion in state R&D credits (mostly indefinite in CA). Both companies face imminent expiration of key R&D and NOL attributes starting in their respective fiscal 2025 periods, though NVIDIA holds a significantly larger base of state R&D credits and federal NOLs with later expiration dates.
